overall: All 29 placeholder functions, the 3 CM848 twin rows, the 76 globals and the 4 enum members were checked against the m68k disassembly (and the CM848 PowerPC code for every twin and counterpart), the e2m records, abs_refs access widths and the RAM dump. Nothing is refuted. The investigator's skipped[] is empty, so nothing stays skipped. Functions: 21 CONFIRMED. 3 names AMENDED (0x31ed2, 0x33754 and 0x34440 also register a PGN 59904 request responder; the repository names such a set-up ...Handler, as in cm550_initializePgn65229Dm4Handler, cm848_initializePgn65234Dm10Handler and CM848's own init...Handler counterparts; ...Buffer is kept for descriptor-only set-ups). 5 plate comments AMENDED: 0x30b0e (its 'progress word 0x877a' is Ghidra's rendering of the jsr return-address push, _DAT_00810ffa = 2 / _DAT_00810ffc = 0x877a, not a progress store), 0x315be (the three ways a record is written), 0x33164 (the set-up seeds bytes 1, 2, 5-6 and 8 only; the RAM dump shows bytes 3 and 7 = 0), 0x33716 (cites the amended set-up name) and 0x34d52 (CM848 has a cranking wet stack timing e2m record). Twins verified: 0x334ec = CM848 0x1b778 (the same 28-byte copy, rebuild and 12 compares at 0/2/3/5/6/8/9/11/12/14/15/27, then the send; neither has a caller), 0x3366a = CM848 0x1b730 (& 0xf0, build, send, schedule (0, 65251, 5000, 110)) and 0x33a1e = CM848 0x26480 (six stores, the 9th set-up in both initializers, FD1 schedule (0, 65213, 1000, 50)). The near twins 0x31ed2 / 0x32c22 / 0x341e6 / 0x344ce stay counterparts, because each differs by one or more stores. The CM550 change helpers 0x333d6 / 0x33460 were hand-traced: they fire on any increase or a drop to 0 and are not a 10 percent test, so the investigator's behaviour names stand. Globals: 69 CONFIRMED and 7 AMENDED: 0x808a7a (trending_storage_record_count reads like the stored count trending_total_sample_count_cal, but TRNOSARQ is the requested sample count), the four 0x801e98-0x801e9e flags (the e2m term is 'trigger is satisfied', and 'window' clashes with the trending interval window names), 0x803e7f (byte[20]: its only use is the 20-byte PGN 65260 descriptor) and 0x804a1a (comment only: 36 rows lie inside the table, not 35; the struct layout is spelled out). APPLY NOTES: (1) create struct trending_sample_record_t (14 bytes: +0 oil_pressure word, +2 boost_pressure word, +4 coolant_temperature word, +6 average_fuel_consumption word, +8 average_load word, +10 time_stamp dword). (2) Create enum TRIP_INFORMATION_ENGINE_STATE (size 2). (3) Delete the 36 bogus rows inside 0x804a1c-0x804f44, 0x804a18 hour_meter_stored_ticks_cal (inside the TRFLUSSR dword) and 0x803698 governor_rpm_error_init_value (inside the PGN 65255 dword). None of these rows has an absolute ROM reference. In the cpp only 0x804a1c and 0x804a20 appear, as the table's field bases. (4) Move part_number_list from 0x803ec2 to 0x803ec5: the part number text starts there, and 0x803ec2 lies inside the new unit number field. (5) Rename the function_definitions.csv prototype rows of 0x333d6 / 0x33460, which are keyed by the old names. (6) Refresh the comments that quote the placeholder names: the j1939_pgn*_tx_message rows, the Phase3 / Phase5 / Phase19 task-set plates, the trip_information_enable / trending_enable bitfield comments and the cm550_initializeTripInformation plate (it quotes fuel_statistics_operating_mode). In CM848, refresh buildPgn65251EngineConfiguration1Payload (0x1b3a0), j1939_pgn65251_payload_previous, j1939_pgn65251_transmit_status and j1939_pgn65213_priority_cal. LEADS (outside the batch): 0x803614 derate_percentage_active is IC1 payload byte 7 (0xff from the set-up, no other access). 0x8034e8 vp44_fso_rpm_fault_counter is EFL/P1 payload byte 1. 0x2f538 cm550_diagnosticDataDump is the J1939 request-responder registration list. 0x2f47e (the 32-entry registrar) and 0x2f4be (the PGN 59904 dispatcher) have no rows. The investigator's descriptor set-up leads (0x31c1a AMB, 0x320f6 CI, 0x33880 ET1, 0x33aea LFC, 0x33eee IC1, 0x3401a PTO, 0x3429a VD, 0x343d2 VH, 0x34334 VEP1, 0x331ae EFL/P1) all check out from the disassembly read here.

verdicts.own_role: Adds one 0.1 s count to TIT3EBTM 0x80615e and TIT2EBTM 0x806176 when engine brake driver 1 (0x80bcf7 bit 0, EBDR1) or drivers 2-6 (0x80bcf9 bit 6, tested five times) is commanded on. The trip task calls it in states 1-3.
verdicts.reason: The disassembly 0x30498-0x304f2 matches the proposal. The six tests are the same as in cm550_ioControlBasedFuelCalculator, which adds JCDR1NCY..JCDR6NCY for EB drivers 1-6, and that identifies the bits. The only caller is bsr.w 0x30a3c in 0x306ca, skipped in state 0. The e2m records resolve as stated. The idle / power take-off siblings 0x30414 / 0x30454 count other records. CM848's trip counters have no engine brake time.

verdicts.own_role: The 100 ms trip information task (Phase19, gated by trip_information_enable). It applies the TIRF trip reset, sets TIEGST (0 rpm 0 / 2 power take-off governor / 1 idle / 3 otherwise) and counts the TIT2TM / TIT3TM run time and TITMT2. It forms TIFU from TIFSRT or TIITFU and the J1939 / J1587 rate words and accumulates lifetime / trip fuel with overflow bits in TIFUSS. It runs the per-state counters, the engine brake and ESP times, then the rpm histogram.
verdicts.reason: Every step was re-traced at 0x306ca-0x30a5c (the state logic at 0x30792-0x307da, fuel at 0x30850-0x309f6, dispatch at 0x30a06-0x30a54). It is the only reader of TIRF 0x80de66 and the only writer of TIEGST besides the start-up clear. CM848 0x523148 does the same job, a trip reset first and then run time, idle and fuel with TIFUSS overflow bits, but with different code and inputs: a counterpart. The name pairs with cm550_initializeTripInformation.

verdicts.own_role: First call of mc68k_runPowerDownSequence (jsr 0x27fb0). With trip information enabled it ORs 0x2|0x80 into TIFUSS for eeprom_write_failure_flag_cal, 0x8|0x200 for system error bit 0x800, and 0x1000|0x2000 for bit 0x1000. Each system error counts only when its fault_processing_enable_flags[0] bit is set.
verdicts.reason: Matches 0x30a5e-0x30adc. The setters of the system error word were checked in cm550_loadParameterBlockAndUpdatePowerDownCounts: 0x800 is set when the consecutive incomplete power-down count passes its limit, and 0x1000 when no parameter block was uploaded. CM848 0x523760 ORs only 0x208 on power_down_data_lost_error: the same role, different code. The RAM dump's TIFUSS = 0x208 shows these bits in use.

verdicts.final_comment: Empty function (a single rts). Its one call is a start-up step of mc68k_applicationMain (jsr at 0x28774), after mc68k_scheduler_init and before the undumped 0x42ad4. No CM848 counterpart is known; an empty body cannot prove one.
verdicts.own_role: A single rts (4e75). Its only reference is jsr 0x28774 in mc68k_applicationMain.
verdicts.reason: The name is confirmed. CM550's empty stubs are cm550_emptyStubFunction4 / 7 / 10, and 11 is unused. The describer's cm550_emptyStartupStub would not single it out, because cm550_emptyPlaceholderInit 0x1ffd0 is another empty start-up call (jsr 0x28864). Comment amended: the 'progress word 0x877a' is the decompiler's view of the jsr pushing its return address (_DAT_00810ffa = 2 / _DAT_00810ffc = 0x877a), not a progress store. The claim about CM848's start-up list is replaced by a statement the code supports.

verdicts.own_role: First call of Phase5 (100 ms). Gated by trending_enable, engine_state != STOPPED and TRITWNAE == 1, it sets four min < x <= max flags (rpm 0x80ccf4, engine load 0x80db5e, IMT filtered_value 0x80a2b2, coolant filtered_value 0x80a336). When all four hold it sets TRTRCD and counts TRTRCDTM to 10 x TRTRSATM, then sets TRTRCDTR. Otherwise it clears all three.
verdicts.reason: Matches 0x31496-0x315bc (cmp.w / bhi / bls window tests, hold timer equality test). It is the only reader of the 126C trigger limits (each has a single cmp.w here). CM848 has no trending records or code. Both roles agree.

verdicts.final_comment: Engine data trending interval: the frame-3 call of executiveFrameInterruptHandler (jsr at 0x1b9ea, once per 40-frame cycle = 200 ms), divided by 300 (counter 0x801ea0) to once a minute. With algorithm_enable_flags_18_cal.trending_enable set and the engine not stopped, it snapshots lifetime_fuel_used at the interval start (e2m 126D +2C TRFLUSSR). It counts TRITTM up to the interval length (2000 minutes while fewer than 3 samples are stored, then 126C +2 TRITTR hours x 60), then runs a capture window a tenth of that length (TRITWNLM / TRITWNTM; TRITWNAE is 1 while it runs). Each minute it adds duty_cycle_monitor_load_factor to TRLDRNT2 and counts TRAVNOCU. Record TRSAIN of trending_storage_table_cal (126E TRSATB, 100 records of 14 bytes) is written in one of three ways. (1) While the window is open and the triggers have held (TRTRCDTR), it stores the oil pressure, boost pressure and coolant temperature filtered values and completes the record at once. (2) When the window closes without that, it zeroes the boost pressure and coolant temperature words. It keeps the oil pressure only when the engine speed, intake manifold temperature and coolant temperature trigger flags are set and the engine load trigger flag is clear; otherwise that word is zeroed too. (3) While any fault_count_table entry is active (status 1 or 3), it writes an all-zero sample when the window closes. Completing a record adds the average fuel consumption (TRAVFLCN: fuel since the snapshot per elapsed hour), the average load (TRLDINAV = TRLDRNT2 / TRAVNOCU) and the time stamp (TRTMST: engine_hour_meter with its low byte replaced by the high byte of throttle_100_fueling, TRTQCDID). It then advances TRSAIN, wrapping at 126C +0 TRNOSARQ, and counts TRNOSATN. When TRNOSATN reaches TRNOSARQ, the count restarts at 3 and the index skips 3, so the first 3 samples are kept. Then the interval restarts. CM848 has no trending feature.
verdicts.own_role: Once a minute: trending interval and capture-window timing, the load accumulation, writing and completing TRSATB sample records, and index / count management.
verdicts.reason: The name is confirmed. It is the only writer of TRSATB and of the interval and window counters. The 24 dumped records decode as 14-byte records (35.5 / 70.4 / 107.6 h, then about 100 h apart to 12460 h). Records 2 and 24 have zeroed sensor words, which is path (2). The plate is amended because 'When the window closes, it adds ...' was wrong for path (1), where the record is completed in the same pass as the sensor write (0x316de, then 0x317c0). The window-end path also zeroes boost / coolant, and keeps oil only under the flag test at 0x31740-0x3175e (the load flag must be clear).

verdicts.own_role: Start-up step (jsr 0x287f8, after cm550_initializeTripInformation). When trending_enable is set and TRRBOC is set, it clears the interval, window and trigger state and TRAVNOCU / TRLDRNT2. It copies TRNOSATN to TRNOSARB and zeroes TRNOSATN, stamps TRRBTMST with engine_hour_meter, and clears TRRBOC.
verdicts.reason: Matches 0x31a68-0x31acc. It is the only reader of TRRBOC 0x8049ea, which nothing in the ROM sets (so a tool sets it), and the only writer of TRNOSARB / TRRBTMST. Both roles agree.

verdicts.own_role: AMB builder: byte 1 (0x801eca) = (ambient_air_pressure_sensor_state.filtered_value x 2 & 0xffff) x 6906 / 1000 >> 7, then cm550_sendCanMessage(0x801ebc). It is scheduled (0, 65269, 1000, 170) at 0x28d74 and registered for 0xfef5 at 0x2f5b6.
verdicts.reason: The descriptor set-up 0x31c1a points the data at 0x801eca and seeds bytes 2-8, so this body is the transmit step. CM848 0x23e8c has the identical formula plus the 0xFE fault substitution and the ambient temperature: a counterpart.

verdicts.own_role: CCVS1 descriptor set-up, the 2nd set-up of mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink (jsr 0x28be2): header 0xfef100, priority 0x803f52 & 7, the source address, DLC 8, data 0x801ee2, status 0x801eea, byte 1 = 0xf3. It then registers 0x31c84 (the CCVS1 builder) for 0xfef1 with the request registrar 0x2f47e.
verdicts.reason: The role and counterpart relation are confirmed: CM848 0x24664 makes the same stores plus ccvs1_cruise_control_state = 7, so it is not a strict twin. The name is amended from ...Buffer to ...Handler. The repository keeps ...Buffer for descriptor-only set-ups (initializePgn65251EngineConfiguration1Buffer, cm550_initializePgn65252ShutdownBuffer, which register nothing). A set-up that also registers the request responder is ...Handler (cm550_initializePgn65229Dm4Handler, cm848_initializePgn65234Dm10Handler, and this function's CM848 counterpart cm848_initPgn65265CruiseSpeedHandler). Unique in CM550.

verdicts.own_role: EBC1 descriptor set-up, the 3rd set-up (jsr 0x28be8): header 0xf00100, priority 0x803f90 & 7, the source address, DLC 5, payload bytes 1 and 3 (0x80347a / 0x80347c) = 0xff, data 0x80347a, status 0x803490. It registers nothing.

verdicts.final_comment: Builds and sends the ECM's EFL/P1 broadcast (PGN 65263). It runs every 500 ms from 130 ms on queue 0, and as the PGN 59904 request responder for 65263. Byte 4 is j1939_pgn65263_engine_oil_pressure (SPN 100, 4 kPa/bit) = (oil_pressure_sensor_state.filtered_value >> 7) x 6906 / 1000 >> 2. Bytes 1, 2, 5-6 and 8 keep the 0xff that the descriptor set-up vp44_engineFluidLevelPGN_65263_Builder stores. Nothing writes bytes 3 and 7 (0 in the RAM dump). It sends j1939_pgn65263_tx_message; nothing in it concerns the VP44. Counterpart of cm848_buildPgn65263EngineFluidLevelPressure1Message, which also sends the fuel delivery and coolant pressures.
verdicts.own_role: EFL/P1 builder: byte 4 (0x8034eb) = oil pressure from A/D record 4, then send 0x8034da. Scheduled (0, 65263, 500, 130) and registered for 0xfeef.
verdicts.reason: The name and relation are confirmed: CM848 0x25eb4 computes the same oil formula and adds the fuel delivery and coolant pressures behind enables and faults. The comment is amended. The set-up 0x331ae writes 0xff only to payload +0, +1, +4..+5 and +7. No code addresses 0x8034ea or 0x8034ee, and the dump has 00 there, so 'the other bytes keep the 0xff' was wrong.

verdicts.own_role: Word compare for the EC1 on-change test, with args (previous, new) (first arg (0xc,a7) = previous). It returns new != 0 when previous is 0. Otherwise d = previous - new, or -previous - new when negative; then q = d / previous (recomputed with -d when negative), and it returns 1 when q x 10 >= 1. Net: 1 for any increase or a drop to 0, 0 for no change or a decrease to non-zero.
verdicts.reason: Hand-traced from the disassembly; it agrees with both earlier emulations. The 0x334ec call sites push new and then previous. CM848 0x1b624 takes |new - old| and passes |diff| >= old or |diff| x 10 / old > 0, a real 10 percent test: different behaviour, so a counterpart. The name states what the code does; the describer's ...ChangedByTenPercent would claim behaviour this code does not have.

verdicts.own_role: The byte version of 0x333d6 (tst.b / move.b on the low bytes of the two word arguments), with the same increase-or-drop-to-zero result. Used for the six byte fields at +2 / +5 / +8 / +0xb / +0xe / +0x1b.
verdicts.reason: The same instruction sequence as 0x333d6 on bytes; its only reference is movea.l #0x33460,a4 in 0x334ec. CM848 0x1b69c is a real 10 percent test: a counterpart.

verdicts.own_role: EC1 send-on-change: copies the 28-byte payload 0x8034f2 to 0x80350e, rebuilds it (0x3320e), compares six word and six byte fields in payload order, and calls 0x3366a on the first change. Nothing calls it.
verdicts.reason: Twin proven against CM848 0x1b778. Both copy 28 bytes (7 x move.l / lswi-stswi 16 + 12) and call the twin buildPgn65251EngineConfiguration1Payload. Both make the same 12 compares at offsets 0, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 27 in the same order, each '== 1' branching to the twin send. Neither has a caller (no jsr / bsr / raw pointer in CM550; no bl / b / raw pointer in either CM848 image). Only the separate compare helpers differ, and those stay prefixed counterparts.

verdicts.own_role: EC1 send: if (0x803538 & 0xf0) == 0, it rebuilds the payload and sends 0x80352a. It is the queue 0 broadcast (0, 65251, 5000, 110) and the last step of the on-change test.
verdicts.reason: Twin proven: CM848 0x1b730 makes the same status test (rlwinm mask 0xf0), the same build call and the send. It has the same schedule (scheduleJ1939PeriodicMessage(0, 0xfee3, 5000, 0x6e)) and the same caller position (bl 0x1b8e4 in the twin on-change). Both rows take the shared name.

verdicts.final_comment: The PGN 59904 request responder for PGN 65253 (HOURS Engine Hours, Revolutions), registered by cm550_initializePgn65253EngineHoursRevolutionsHandler. Bytes 1-4 are j1939_pgn65253_total_engine_hours (SPN 247, 0.05 h/bit, low byte first) = total_engine_operating_time (e2m 117F +20 TITMT2, 0.1 s counts) x 20 / 36000. Bytes 5-8 (SPN 249 revolutions) stay 0xff. It sends j1939_pgn65253_tx_message. CM848 has no PGN 65253 message.
verdicts.own_role: HOURS request responder: cm550_scaleByRatio(0x804fc0, 20, 36000), byteSwap32 into 0x803548, then send 0x80353a.

verdicts.own_role: ET1 builder: byte 1 coolant (A/D record 6) and byte 2 fuel temperature (vp44_fuel_temperature >> 4), each deg F to deg C + 40 clamped 0 / 250, bytes 3-4 = 0xffff, then send 0x803552. Scheduled (0, 65262, 1000, 430) and registered by 0x33880.

Both are the 9th set-up of their J1939 initializers, and both FD1 builders are scheduled (0, 65213, 1000, 50). Neither firmware has another use of the name.

Byte 6 = 0xcc / 0xdc from 0x80bcd0 bit 4 (remote PTO switch, switch 21), |1 from 0x80bcd5 bit 4 (PTO on). Byte 7 = 0xcc / 0xdc from bit 0 (resume), |1 from bit 2 (set). Then send 0x803618. Scheduled (0, 65264, 100, 150) and registered at 0x2f5aa.

The name is amended to ...Handler because this set-up registers the request responder; CM848's counterpart is likewise cm848_initPgn65260VehicleIdHandler. See 0x31ed2. Unique in CM550.

verdicts.own_role: PGN 65279 descriptor set-up, the 19th set-up (jsr 0x28c48): header 0xfeff00, priority 0x803f94 & 7, the source address, DLC 1, data 0x8036ac, status 0x8036c2. It registers nothing.
verdicts.reason: Matches 0x344ce-0x34510. CM848 0x26efc makes the same stores plus seven 0xff payload stores: a counterpart. There is no VP44 access. The builder 0x34496 sends 1 when 0x80bcf6 bit 2 (LCWFLP) is on.

verdicts.final_comment: Wet stack timing, the third call of cm550_runEvery4FramesTaskSetPhase3 (20 ms). wet_stack_timing_advance (e2m 1077 +0 WSTA 'timing advance as commanded by wet stack') = the base wet_stack_timing_base_value_0_120 (1077 +4 WSADTA: the larger of the intake manifold and coolant temperature table values, set by 0x34cc4) while final_fueling is at or below 1074 +2 WSMXLMFL. Above that, it is the base minus wet_stack_timing_ramp_rate (1074 +4 WSTARM) x (final_fueling - WSMXLMFL) / 100. The result is held at or above wet_stack_timing_advance_minimum (140A +0 WSTAMN). cm550_applyWetStackTimingAdvance then raises the timing command to it. CM848 has no counterpart: its e2m has only a cranking wet stack timing record (Crank_Wet_Stack_Timing CKWSTA), and no CM848 function or global handles wet stack timing.
verdicts.own_role: WSTA 0x80dee4 = WSADTA 0x80dee8, minus WSTARM x (final_fueling - WSMXLMFL) / 100 when final_fueling > WSMXLMFL. The result is then floored at WSTAMN 0x808ac4 (a signed compare against the zero-extended minimum).
verdicts.reason: The name is confirmed. The code matches 0x34d52-0x34db8, and the only reference is jsr 0x1b61e (Phase3, third call). There is no VP44 access, so the vp44_ prefix goes. The comment's last sentence is amended: CM848's labelled e2m does have a wet stack timing record (CKWSTA, cranking), so 'no wet stack timing algorithm' overstated it.

verdicts.own_role: When j1939_pgn65251_transmit_status & 0xf0 == 0, it calls buildPgn65251EngineConfiguration1Payload and cm848_sendJ1939Message. It is the (0, 65251, 5000, 110) broadcast, and 0x1b778 calls it (bl 0x1b8e4).
verdicts.reason: PowerPC 0x1b730-0x1b774 matches CM550 0x3366a step for step. The one bl caller is 0x1b8e4, and the scheduler entry is in cm848_j1939_system_init. Shared name.

verdicts.own_role: Copies 28 bytes 0x3fa7f8 -> 0x3fa814 and calls bl 0x1b3a0. It then makes 12 helper compares (word 0x1b624 / byte 0x1b69c alternating) at 0, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 27; on the first '== 1' it calls bl 0x1b730. No caller.
verdicts.reason: The same steps, order and offsets as CM550 0x334ec. No b / bl or raw pointer reaches it in cm848_rom.bin or cm848_flash2_live.bin. Shared name.

verdicts.own_role: FD1 descriptor at 0x3fae28: stw 0xfebd00, priority & 7 << 2 into byte 0, source address into byte 3, length 2, data 0x3fae20, status 0x3fae36. The 9th set-up (bl from flash2 0x53926c).
verdicts.reason: Six stores identical to CM550 0x33a1e, the same initializer position and the same FD1 builder schedule. Shared name.
e2m 1216 +38 TIT3EBTM, length 4. addq.l at 0x304e6 and clr.l at 0x3075c (trip reset) are its only references. The name pairs with trip_engine_run_time.
e2m 1216 +50 TIT2EBTM, length 4. Its only reference is addq.l at 0x304ec; the trip reset does not clear it.

e2m 1216 +28 TIFUSS, length 4, the same Calterm record as CM848 trip_information_fault_status_cal. All 13 references are long (ori.l / clr.l) in 0x306ca and 0x30a5e, with the bits as listed. The dump value is 0x208. Outside the EEPROM image, so no _cal. The old name described only the overflow bits.
e2m 1215 +14 TIRF, length 2. cmpi.w #1 at 0x306ee and clr.w at 0x306fa are the only references. It has CM848's name for the same record. The existing row has a type and an empty name.
e2m 1216 +3C TIT3TM, length 4 (CM848 trip_engine_run_time_cal is the same record). Long accesses at 0x3080c / 0x3081e and clr.l at 0x30762; the dump equals the lifetime count (12567 h, never reset).
e2m 1216 +14 TIT2TM, length 4 (CM848 lifetime_engine_run_time_cal). Four long accesses, all in 0x306ca. It is not a sample counter.

e2m 1216 +58 TIT3EZTM ('ESP high HP mode'), length 4. addq.l at 0x30a48 while SPTU 0x80d2b4 != 0; clr.l at 0x30768. ESP is spelled out as electronic smart power, as in cm550_updateElectronicSmartPowerTau.
e2m 1216 +5C TIT2EZTM, length 4. Its only reference is addq.l at 0x30a4e.

e2m 1215 +12 TIEGST, length 2, range 0-3 ('ENG_OFF, IDLE, PTO' in the full label of another e2m). Word stores 0 / 2 / 1 / 3 and compares with 3 / 1 / 2, through a4 in 0x306ca, plus clr.w in 0x30ade. The new enum (size 2) carries the members.

e2m 117F +20 TITMT2, length 4. Long stores at 0x30836 / 0x3084a; long reads at 0x33724 and 0xf68a (0x35f9x is the parameter ID table entry). 0x804fc0 is past the EEPROM image end 0x804f93, so no _cal.
e2m 1217 +2 TIT2TMOF, length 4. sub.l at 0x30826 and add.l at 0x30844 (long). Inside the EEPROM image, so _cal. The dump value is 0.
e2m 117F +0 TIGAT2 'total fuel consumed by engine' (0.125 gal), length 4. Written by move.l from lifetime_fuel_used at 0x309ec; long reads at 0x33aa8 and 0xf6b2. No _cal (outside the image).

e2m 117F +4 TIGAT3, length 4. A move.l copy of trip_fuel_used at 0x309f6, clr.l in the trip reset 0x3078c, and long reads at 0x33a7c / 0xf370. The name follows the record text; the comment states that it is the report copy.

verdicts.final_comment: e2m 126C +0 TRNOSARQ 'user-specified number of engine data samples taken by trending feature' (0-100; 100 in the dump): the number of trending_storage_table_cal records in use. cm550_runTrendingIntervalAndStoreSamples wraps the record index trending_write_index_cal at it. When the stored count trending_total_sample_count_cal reaches it, that count is set to 3 and the index moves on by 3.
verdicts.reason: The address, the word width (cmp.w (a2) at 0x318b8 / 0x318ce / 0x318e6, sub.w at 0x318ec; 0x366fc / 0x36700 are the parameter ID table) and the role are confirmed. The name is amended: 'trending_storage_record_count' reads as the number of records stored, which is TRNOSATN (trending_total_sample_count_cal). This record is the requested capacity (the RQ in TRNOSARQ). Unique in CM550.
e2m 126C +2 TRITTR (HRS, 1-790), length 2. Its only reference is move.w at 0x31622, followed by x 60. The dump value is 100, and the dumped records are about 100 h apart.

e2m 126C +4 TRTRSATM (SEC), length 2. One move.w at 0x31582, then x 10 against the 0.1 s timer. The X_time (limit) / X_timer (counter) pair with trending_trigger_hold_timer_cal follows CM550 precedent (crank_jump_start_time / _timer).
e2m 126C +6 TRESMX. Its only reference is cmp.w at 0x314de (rpm > it clears the flag). The dump value is 18800 = 2350 rpm.
e2m 126C +8 TRESMN. Its only reference is cmp.w at 0x314ec (rpm <= it clears the flag). The dump value is 16000 = 2000 rpm. The old name rpm_divisor_value has no basis.
e2m 126C +A TRPCLDMX. Its only reference is cmp.w at 0x31502 against engine_load_at_current_speed_percent.
e2m 126C +C TRPCLDMN. Its only reference is cmp.w at 0x31510. The dump value is 0x5f00 = 95 percent.
e2m 126C +E TRIMTPMX. Its only reference is cmp.w at 0x31526 against intake_manifold_temperature_sensor_state.filtered_value (0x80a2b2). The dump value is 255 F.
e2m 126C +10 TRIMTPMN. Its only reference is cmp.w at 0x3152e. The dump value is 70 F.
e2m 126C +12 TRCQMX. Its only reference is cmp.w at 0x31544 against coolant_temperature_sensor_state.filtered_value (0x80a336). The dump value is 255 F.
e2m 126C +14 TRCQMN. Its only reference is cmp.w at 0x3154c. The dump value is 170 F.

The role and width are confirmed: word stores through a0 in 0x31496 and tst.w at 0x31740 in 0x315be; working RAM, no e2m record. The name is amended to the e2m's own term ('engine speed trigger is satisfied in trending'), next to trending_all_triggers_satisfied_flag_cal. 'in_window' collides with the trending interval window names (trending_interval_window_*), which mean the time window.

Word stores through a1 in 0x31496; tst.w at 0x31748 in 0x315be, where at the window end the oil pressure is kept only while this flag is clear. The name is amended for the same reason as 0x801e98 (the e2m 'loading trigger is satisfied').
Word stores through a3 in 0x31496; tst.w at 0x31750. The name is amended for the same reason as 0x801e98 (the e2m 'IMT trigger is satisfied').
Word stores through a2 in 0x31496; tst.w at 0x31758. The name is amended for the same reason as 0x801e98 (the e2m 'coolant temp trigger is satisfied').
a1 = 0x801ea0: addq.w / cmpi.w #300 / clr.w at 0x315da-0x315e4 are its only uses. 300 calls x 200 ms = 1 minute.
a4 = 0x801ea2: move.b #1 at 0x316de / 0x31790, tst.b at 0x317c0, and clr.b at 0x31a60 at the end of every pass. Byte.
e2m 126D +0 TRRBOC, length 2. tst.w at 0x31a74 and clr.w at 0x31aa6 are its only references. EEPROM image, so _cal. The dump value is 0.
e2m 126D +2 TRRBTMST (SEC 0.2, length 4). Its only reference is move.l from engine_hour_meter at 0x31abc. It is not a pointer.
e2m 126D +6 TRTMST (length 4). move.l stores at 0x3186a / 0x319aa (engine_hour_meter & 0xffffff00) and or.l reads at 0x31896 / 0x319d6 into each record's time stamp.
e2m 126D +A TRITTM (HRS 0.01667 = 1 minute). Word accesses at 0x31600 / 0x31638 / 0x3163e / 0x318f2 / 0x31a7c. The dump value is 6000 (100 h).
e2m 126D +C TRITWNLM 'limit for interval window counter set to 10% of trending interval'. move.w after divs.l #10 at 0x31650; cmp.w at 0x3166a. The dump value is 600.
e2m 126D +E TRITWNTM 'elapsed time during trending interval window' (minutes). Word accesses as listed. The old name trending_sample_phase_counter_cal is replaced.
e2m 126D +14 TRNOSARB. Its only reference is the move.w destination at 0x31aac. The dump value is 100.

e2m 126D +1A TRITWNAE 'flag set when time conditions are satisfied for trending (interval window)'. Ten word accesses in 0x31496 / 0x315be / 0x31a68. It is the capture window flag, not a capture-active state of its own.
e2m 126D +1C TRITWNAL '(n-1) trending interval window' flag. cmpi.w #1 at 0x31734 / 0x31924; move.w from 0x804a04 at 0x31a56; clr.w at 0x31a9a.
e2m 126D +1E TRTRCD. move.w #1 at 0x3156c and clr.w at 0x315a6 are its only references.

e2m 126D +20 TRAVNOCU 'counter used as no. of samples in trending avg. load computation'. addq.w at 0x31682; it is the divu divisor at 0x31834; cleared at 0x318a6 / 0x319e6 / 0x31aa0. It is not an output control timer.
e2m 126D +22 TRLDRNT2 (length 4). add.l of duty_cycle_monitor_load_factor at 0x31690; move.l at 0x3182c; clr.l at 0x31910 / 0x31a50 / 0x31ac6.
e2m 126D +26 TRLDINAV. move.w at 0x3183e (accumulator / count), copied into record +8.

e2m 126D +28 TRTQCDID 'holds max value of torque curve in use when trending data is written'. Word store of throttle_100_fueling & 0xff00 at 0x3187a / 0x319ba; reads at 0x3188e / 0x319ce. The dump value is 0x600.
e2m 126D +2A TRAVFLCN (GPH 0.125). move.w at 0x31804, clr.w at 0x3180c, copied into record +6. The dump value is 24 = 3 GPH.

e2m 126D +2C TRFLUSSR (length 4). move.l from lifetime_fuel_used at 0x31608; sub.l at 0x317fa. The dump value is 241371 x 0.125 = 30171 gal. The undefined row 0x804a18 hour_meter_stored_ticks_cal lies inside the dword and has no reference in the ROM or the cpp; delete it.

verdicts.final_comment: e2m 126E +0 TRSATB 'trending feature long term storage table' (1400 bytes, 0x804a1a-0x804f91, EEPROM image): 100 records of 14 bytes, written only by cm550_runTrendingIntervalAndStoreSamples at index trending_write_index_cal (TRSAIN). New struct trending_sample_record_t (14 bytes): +0 oil_pressure word (oil_pressure_sensor_state.filtered_value), +2 boost_pressure word (boost_pressure_sensor_state.filtered_value), +4 coolant_temperature word (coolant_temperature_sensor_state.filtered_value), +6 average_fuel_consumption word (the TRAVFLCN copy, 0.125 GPH), +8 average_load word (the TRLDINAV copy, 0.01 percent), +10 time_stamp dword (TRTMST: engine_hour_meter, 0.2 s, with its low byte replaced by the high byte of throttle_100_fueling). RAM dump: 24 records decode (35.5 / 70.4 / 107.6 h, then about every 100 h from 10427 h to 12460 h; coolant 185-199 F, 2.25-3.75 GPH, load 23-36 percent). The 36 undefined rows inside the table (0x804a1c engine_runtime_total_counter_cal through 0x804f44 diagnostic_active_fault_counter_cal) have no absolute reference and are deleted.
verdicts.reason: The name, the address and the struct type are confirmed. The base addresses 0x804a1a / 0x804a1c / 0x804a1e / 0x804a20 / 0x804a22 / 0x804a24, with index x 14 and word / long accesses, prove the layout, and no other e2m record resolves inside the table (only 126E is based there). The comment is amended to give the struct layout in place of 'layout in notes' and to correct the count of rows inside the table from 35 to 36. In the cpp only 0x804a1c / 0x804a20 appear, as this table's field bases.

movea.l #0x801f12 at 0x32054 with byte stores to +0x27, and the descriptor data pointer and DLC 0x28 at 0x32120. No row lies in 0x801f12-0x801f39. It has CM848's name; CM848's 44-byte struct does not fit (4-byte serial number).
5-byte copy loops at 0x32062 / 0x27834 / 0x278e8 (byte reads). The dump has CMMNS (the J1939 make code) at DAT_PLAT +2. Dataplate inside the EEPROM image, so _cal.
17-byte loops (cmpi.b #0x11) at 0x32084 / 0x27860 / 0x27904. The dump is 'ISB 195' padded to 17 bytes (0x803dd1-0x803de1).
4-byte loops at 0x320a8 / 0x2788c / 0x27920, read bytewise. The dump has 03 5e 4b 37 (56511287, an 8-digit Cummins ESN).

Its only use is the 10-byte loop at 0x320cc. The dump has 10 spaces (0x803ebb-0x803ec4) and the part number digits from 0x803ec5. The field covers the undefined row part_number_list 0x803ec2, which has no ROM or cpp reference; move that row to 0x803ec5 in the same change, as the investigator notes.

verdicts.final_comment: The VIN text field of the EEPROM image dataplate (e2m 0006 DAT_PLAT +0xb5; spaces in the dump). Its only use: cm550_initializePgn65260VehicleIdentificationHandler points the PGN 65260 descriptor at it with data length 20. The name matches CM848's vehicle_vin_string_cal (CM848 also copies 20 bytes from it for PGN 65260).
verdicts.reason: The name is confirmed. The type is amended to byte[20]: the only access is the descriptor at 0x3446a with DLC 0x14 at 0x34464, which sends 20 bytes from 0x803e7f. CM848 likewise copies 0x14 bytes, and its next string starts 20 bytes later. Nothing in CM550 uses 17 bytes, and no row lies in 0x803e7f-0x803e92. The comment now cites the amended set-up name.
move.b at 0x31c02 is the only write; the set-up 0x31c1a uses it as the data pointer (payload byte 1). It has CM848's name.
Its only reference is move.b at 0x33196; it is payload +3 (byte 4) of the buffer at 0x8034e8. The dump value is 0x56.
move.l at 0x3373e (byte-swapped hours) and the data pointer at 0x33754; bytes 5-8 are seeded with 0xff separately. Dword.
clr.b / move.b through a0 = 0x803560 at 0x33802-0x33818; it is the data pointer in 0x33880. The dump value is 0x88 = 96 C.
clr.b / move.b (1,a1) at 0x3384a-0x33864, from vp44_fuel_temperature. Byte.
Its only write is move.w #0xffff,(2,a1) at 0x33868 (SPN 175 not available). Word.
move.l at 0x33aa2 and the data pointer at 0x33b14 (SPN 182, bytes 1-4).
Its only reference is move.l at 0x33ace (SPN 250, bytes 5-8).
move.b d0,(1,a2) with a2 = 0x80360e at 0x33e8e (SPN 102, byte 2). Byte.
clr.b / move.b through a3 = 0x803610 at 0x33ec0-0x33ed6 (SPN 105, byte 3). The dump value is 0x56 = 46 C.
Byte stores (3,a2) / (4,a2) at 0x33f80 / 0x33f7a from byteSwap16(power_take_off_requested_engine_speed) (SPN 187, bytes 4-5).
move.b #0xdc / #0xcc,(5,a2) and ori.b #1,(5,a2) (byte 6: SPN 978 bits 5-6, SPN 980 bits 1-2). The dump value is 0xcc.
move.b #0xdc / #0xcc,(a4) and ori.b #1,(a4) with a4 = 0x80362c (byte 7: SPN 982 resume, SPN 984 set). The dump value is 0xcc.
move.l at 0x3425a and the data pointer at 0x342c4 (SPN 244).
Its only reference is move.l at 0x34284 (SPN 245).
Its only references are the data pointer at 0x343fc and moveq #-1 / move.l at 0x34414 (SPN 246 not available; 0xffffffff in the dump). There is no protection role.
Its only reference is move.l at 0x343bc (SPN 248). The undefined row 0x803698 governor_rpm_error_init_value lies inside the dword with no ROM or cpp reference; delete it.
move.b #1 / clr.b through a0 = 0x8036ac in the builder 0x34496 (0x80bcf6 bit 2 LCWFLP); it is the data pointer at 0x34500 (DLC 1). It has CM848's name.

move.b #0xff at 0x32c5a (byte) and movea.l #0x80347a as the payload base in 0x32bbc / 0x32c28 (the data pointer). Never anything but 0xff. The payload_byte_N form has CM848 precedent (j1939_pgn65264_payload_byte_6). There is no lift pump role.
Its only write is move.b #0xff,(2,a0) with a0 = 0x80347a at 0x32c62; there is no absolute reference, so it is not a pointer.

e2m 140A +0 WSTAMN 'low limitation of wet_stack_timing value' (length 2). a3 = 0x808ac4 in 0x34d52: a zero-extended move.w compare and a move.w floor. The dump value is 0x1bc = about -8 deg. Outside the image, so no _cal.
e2m 1074 +4 WSTARM. Its only reference is move.w then mulu.l at 0x34d88. It is not a VP44 fault threshold.
e2m 1077 +0 WSTA. The only writer is 0x34d52 (move.w through a2); cm550_applyWetStackTimingAdvance reads it at 0x34dcc.

Stored by clr.w (a4) at 0x3079a when current_engine_rpm_filtered == 0, and by the clr.w in cm550_initializeTripInformation. tst.w at 0x307de then clears the rate words and the fault timer and skips all accumulators. The e2m label is ENG_OFF.

move.w #1 at 0x307d4: road speed 0 with VSSVF (117D +2A) = 1, or final_fueling_state 11 (low speed governor) with VSSVF != 1. The compare with 1 at 0x30a12 runs 0x30414 (idle time and fuel). The e2m label is IDLE.
move.w #2 at 0x307a8 when power_take_off_governor_active_flag == 1. The compare with 2 at 0x30a18 runs 0x30454 (power take-off time and fuel). The e2m label is PTO, spelled out.

move.w #3 at 0x307da, the default. The compare with 3 at 0x30a0c adds the drive fuel (0x303d4 on trip_drive_fuel_used, TIT3VSFU 'engine not at idle and PTO not active'). No other store or compare of 0x80de64 exists in the ROM.
